description:
FILED s404 (Opus 5), found while probing the #351 repair's BREAKING cases (it is
the case the repair must NOT touch, and it turned out to be broken already).

    use constant PI => 6;
    print PI / 2, "\n";        perl: 3       PCL: statement DROPPED (no output)

Announced by the drop line:

    PCL: statement dropped at F line 2: print PI / 2, "\n"; -- Bug. Fell
    through. Missing case: []

PRE-EXISTING, verified against a worktree at HEAD before the s404 repairs: the
identical drop, identical message.  NOT a PPI bug — PPI tokenizes it correctly
(Word(print) Word(PI) Operator(/) Number(2) Operator(,) Quote), so this is
PCL's own PExpr: a bareword CONSTANT as the first element of a paren-less list
operator's argument list, followed by a binary operator.

SHAPES (probe them all before fixing):
  print PI / 2, "\n";      DROPPED     (perl 3)
  print PI, "\n";          works
  print PI + 1, "\n";      ? (probe)
  my  = PI / 2;         ? (probe)
  sub g () { 10 } print g / 2, "\n";   DROPPED the same way (probed s404)

WHERE: the ``/term region owns the paren-less list-operator argument
run, so per the standing rule this waits for Option B phase 2 (task #153)
unless the fix is provably outside that region — check first whether the
constant is being consumed as a TERM-with-no-operator by the same code path
that #266's callable classifier feeds.

BAR: perl-probed shapes above; a guard row in Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t; the
drop census falls by the affected files (`tools/drop-census.pl`).


SECOND FLAVOUR, worse, found by the same probe (s404): a constant as the first
word of a paren-less `print` is taken for a FILEHANDLE, with NO drop and NO
announcement — the output simply goes nowhere:

    use constant PI => 6;
    print PI + 1, "\n";      perl: 7      PCL: (nothing)

emits

    (p-print :fh 'PI 1 "\n")

so `PI` became the filehandle and `+ 1` the list.  perl resolves the same
ambiguity with the symbol table: PI is a known sub (a constant), so it is
`print(PI() + 1, "\n")`.  This is the #266 question ("a bare NAME is a CALL
only where it is CALLABLE") asked at the print-filehandle site — PExpr's
`_is_known_callable` already answers it for two other callers, which is where
the fix should key.

MEASURED shapes (perl vs PCL, s404):
    print PI + 1, "\n";        perl 7   PCL nothing      (filehandle misread)
    print PI / 2, "\n";        perl 3   PCL DROPPED      (announced)
    my $x = PI / 2;            perl 3   PCL 3            ok
    print((PI / 2), "\n");     perl 3   PCL 3            ok
    my @a = (PI / 2);          perl 3   PCL 3            ok
    sub g () { 10 } print g / 2, "\n";   perl 5   PCL DROPPED

subject: SILENT DROP: `print CONSTANT / 2` — a constant followed by division is dropped whole
